recommendation: Keep the source fix. It completes the approved FHIR-34152 documentation wiring without duplicating the full pattern examples page or reopening FHIR-36700's separate detailed pattern wording decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-34152 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked FHIR-core to better explain what pattern does, especially the difference between fixed[x] and pattern[x] with examples involving ids, extensions, and matching behavior, with links from the detailed descriptions.
initial_application: Historical commit 5ec590094792f8d1ca97dc89ab06eb362c610193 applied part of FHIR-34152 by revising profiling discriminator text and linking slicing-by-value guidance to pattern examples. Related issue FHIR-36700 was later applied by 44ed2366be24968481e1dc367d04cff3be43df0d, adding the ElementDefinition pattern examples page and expanded pattern[x] wording. The remaining FHIR-34152 gap was the profiling-page fixed-vs-pattern anchor and fixed[x]/pattern[x] detailed-description link wiring.
additional_context: ElementDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini and its examples/detailed descriptions are listed in source/hierarchy.xml, so the edited ElementDefinition spreadsheet source and profiling page feed the current build. FHIR-I 2021-10-19 minutes record creation and approval of FHIR-34152. Quoted Zulip and Confluence FTS searches found no conflicting community discussion. FHIR-36700 is tightly related but already represented on the combined branch and was not decided again.
reconciliation: Changed source/profiling.html to add a Fixed and Pattern Values section immediately before Slicing, explaining exact fixed matching, partial pattern matching, ids/extensions/additional codings, and repeating-element behavior. Updated source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml so ElementDefinition.fixed[x] and ElementDefinition.pattern[x] detailed descriptions link to that new section, while pattern[x] keeps its examples link.
